title: Attempt-log decoder strictness asymmetry: one key-less entry silently empties the whole attempts array on the wire
evidence:
shared/src/shared/reference_call.gleam:408-414: "pub fn attempt_decoder() -> decode.Decoder(ReferenceCallAttempt) {
  use at <- decode.field("at", decode.string)
  use channel <- decode.field("channel", decode.string)
  use outcome <- decode.field("outcome", decode.string)
  use detail <- decode.field("detail", decode.string)
  decode.success(ReferenceCallAttempt(at:, channel:, outcome:, detail:))}" vs server/src/reference_checks/sweep.gleam:816-822 ("use at <- decode.optional_field("at", "", decode.string)" x4) and server/src/reference_checks/result.gleam:515-520 (same optional_field pattern); the handler's parse_attempt_log (application_detail_handler.gleam:1203-1213) maps any single decode failure to [] for the whole log.
detail: The sweep's internal parsers tolerate missing keys (optional_field, '' default); the new shared codec requires all four. A single stored entry missing any key (future/legacy writer) makes the payload's attempts silently decode to [] while the warm-handoff render still shows it.
recommended_fix: Align the shared attempt_decoder with the sweep's tolerance (optional_field with '' defaults) so a partial entry degrades per-entry instead of wiping the whole log.
